feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear domain focus, solid progression, and relevant public-sector scale. It reads professionally and is rich in substance, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by emphasizing outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications leadership.  
- Credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with internal advancement signals trust, growth, and increasing scope.  
- Good use of scale indicators: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add weight.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe duties (“led,” “supported,” “advised”) without showing business/user impact, efficiency gains, or measurable results.  
- Fix style consistency and minor writing issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s” usage is uneven; punctuation in lists is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler for education. No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and add 1–2 concrete signals of scale or scope from recent roles.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language like “leading” or “delivering.”
- Streamline the list of focus areas so it feels less like a skills section; group related items.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years guiding web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise platforms, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations, with recent experience overseeing a 10,000+ page Drupal migration, analytics modernization, and cross-channel digital operations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” and the long capability list repeat content already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The subtitle already establishes leadership focus, so the intro should emphasize impact and scale rather than restating functions.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened, made more distinctive, and aligned in style around higher-value capability areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use broader, less repetitive phrases: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Cross-channel communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Shorten “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content discovery” for clarity and specificity.
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “systems,” “operations,” and “experiences” unless intentionally grouped.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section overlaps heavily with the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming to 6 items or using it only if ATS keyword coverage is needed.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already strongly established in the header and work experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like a repeat of the experience section and is slightly too dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp line.
- Use parallel verbs and style: “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched,” “Produced”; also hyphenate consistently (“bill-level,” “10-by-20-foot”).
- Make each project more specific with one differentiator or result, e.g., audience, platform, scale, or purpose.
- Consider this tighter version: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search—Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level chat. We Are Counties Microsite—Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources. Organization Anniversary Campaign—Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10-by-20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series—Produced a recurring advocacy video program across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI search, microsites, and advocacy video closely overlap with current/frecent work bullets; keep footer phrasing shorter and more portfolio-like.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily across the block; vary verbs slightly if space allows.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact outcomes and make the freelance/full-time nature feel more like a strategic engagement than generic support.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client type: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and content operations improvements.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: “Led,” “Built,” “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Established.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets, e.g.:
- Led Drupal-based campaign and storytelling builds, including microsites, modular content components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Built communications workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve cross-channel coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Directed CMS/front-end enhancements and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Shaped an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics if possible: site size, users, publishers, campaign launches, time saved, engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “enterprise web improvement” repeat the header and NACo role; keep this entry focused on new consulting impact.
- AI search and microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel bullet and add results if available: include email open/click growth, social engagement, audience growth, or campaign performance rather than “tens of thousands/thousands.”
- Rephrase ops/analytics bullets for business value: “Built reporting stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving leadership visibility and decision-making”; “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-team planning workflows to improve consistency and efficiency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role.
- Video production/studio language may duplicate the Recent Projects/earlier NACo multimedia entries.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support than leadership. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and operational improvements distinct from the later director role and earlier producer role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with ownership and scale: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination for advocacy and member communications.”
- Combine newsletter/video bullets into sharper impact statements: “Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders” and “Produced a weekly advocacy video series that established video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Make cross-functional work more concrete: “Built tighter editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving alignment and publishing cadence.”
- Replace “helped improve” with stronger action + outcome if possible: “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed and cross-team coordination.” Add metrics if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; differentiate this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.
- Website/email/social oversight overlaps with the 2022–2024 director role; avoid repeating governance, analytics, and broad channel leadership language.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership themes not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content operations” or “digital modernization” to better reflect recent, higher-impact work.
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid mixing broad strategy terms with lower-level execution language.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable proof points for experience bullets rather than skills lists.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also echoes the header and multiple NACo roles; keep only if this specialization is important for target roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools under impact-oriented themes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and platform integrations • Workflow automation and Airtable systems • AI-enabled search experiences**
- Remove lower-priority or older-signal items here: cut **jQuery** unless required for target roles.
- Consider dropping **WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages** from this topline item unless they are central to current job targets; keep them in “Technical + IT” instead.
- If space allows, make one phrase more outcome-oriented: **Enterprise web modernization and technical execution** instead of just **CMS modernization**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and recent project content; keep wording consistent but avoid repeating it everywhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic capability over software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • Leadership reporting • SEO and performance analysis • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Put the most senior/value-add items first: KPI design, executive reporting, analytics strategy, optimization.
- Tighten phrasing: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboarding” for clearer business impact.
- If accurate, add one measurable angle in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, such as dashboard adoption, reporting cadence, or decision-making improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating the full tool stack here if it already appears in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and outcomes-oriented.

Suggested edit
- Rename to emphasize leadership and delivery scope: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Event Delivery**
- Tighten and elevate phrasing: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and multi-camera studio systems • Studio buildout and operations • Virtual event production**
- If space allows, add scale/context instead of tool-only terms: e.g., **In-house studio production for advocacy programming and recurring event coverage**
- Consider replacing “video production and editing” with **End-to-end video production** to signal planning through delivery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” partially duplicate **Multimedia production and livestream operations** in Core Competencies.
- “Studio operations” and production capability are already evidenced in the **Director of Digital Media** role; avoid repeating identical wording.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be tightened to emphasize the most relevant, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling depth: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If you want cleaner phrasing, rename the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for brevity and standard terminology.
- Keep only platforms you can credibly discuss in interviews; if GitHub Pages was minor, consider dropping it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one list or making this version more specific.
- Drupal already appears prominently across recent roles, so avoid over-weighting older/lighter platforms.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from basic languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group tools by use case for clarity: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Keep only tools you actively used in recent roles/projects; if possible, swap in stronger specifics like “custom Drupal theming,” “CMS troubleshooting,” or “search/API implementation”
- Consider this rewrite: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and CMS integrations • Google Tag Manager • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization unless implementation is a core selling point.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so this item should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to grouped systems: “Workflow automation & collaboration: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; team operations: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Prioritize the most relevant tools first; if space is tight, cut weaker/older items like Basecamp or Trello unless used recently.
- If accurate, add a qualifier showing application: “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and automated communications workflows.”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clearer alignment with your recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if they were central to operational systems, not just everyday communication.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for this profile, but the item is too bare and doesn’t reflect the scale of email operations shown in recent NACo roles. It should emphasize enterprise/member communications rather than read like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely depth/relevance: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief: **Higher Logic (weekly newsletters, member communications at scale) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration/segmentation) • Mailchimp**
- Keep naming consistent and concise; consider shortening to **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights (Journeys)** unless the full product name is important for ATS.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating outcomes here unless adding tool-specific depth.
- “Engagement” is broad; if no CRM/community use beyond email, “Email Marketing Platforms” may be cleaner.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In a technical section, make it tighter and more tool-specific, with methods only if they’re core strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting**
- Replace **SEO** with **Google Search Console** or **SEO analysis**; “SEO” is broad compared with the other platform/tool entries.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI/dashboard reporting** or **Executive reporting** to sound more outcome-oriented and less vague.
- Order by strongest/recent tools first; if GA4/BigQuery/Power BI were central in the NACo role, keep those at the front.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly repeats the “Topline Skills” analytics list; consider keeping the broader capability framing there and making this section strictly tools/platforms.
- If you keep **A/B testing** here, avoid repeating optimization language elsewhere unless tied to a measurable result.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” and team-building contributions without repeating leadership claims covered in 2018–2024 roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and outcomes: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Tighten the second sentence around concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand NACo’s in-house communications capacity.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics or metrics if available: number of livestreams, cadence of video series, audience growth, or workflow/time savings.
- Clarify supervision modestly: use “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” only if people management is worth keeping.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already emphasized more strongly in later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts,” while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and impact: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; produced digital and multimedia content to extend reach and engagement.”
- Make the podcast achievement the centerpiece: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes, audience/downloads, stakeholder groups served, or projects delivered.
- Consider a two-bullet format for clarity:
- Coordinated innovation/research projects supporting county policy and program initiatives.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast and produced supporting multimedia content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo media roles; keep this entry focused on the podcast launch and innovation/project coordination.
- Avoid broad “digital communications” language here since stronger, more recent leadership examples already cover that.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
